mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a steady, decelerating narrowing of its negative baseline gap over the last four weeks (-15.4 to -13.6), indicating organic recovery momentum that should continue into the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each week from -15.4 to -13.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite the prior four-week improving trend persisting through the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week deterioration in TRANSIT mobility beyond historical noise levels signals renewed mobility restrictions or public caution, which spills over to suppress retail and recreation visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 1.5 points week-on-week and remains below -36
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from -35.1 to -36.7 in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT crossing below -36 at the decision point, or RETAIL_REC keeps improving regardless of TRANSIT's dip.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL time (around +4.4 to +4.9) combined with flat WORKPLACES mobility (around -12 to -13) indicates households remain anchored at home without resuming office-linked routines, jointly suppressing discretionary retail trips over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 4.4 and 4.9 while WORKPLACES stayed between -13.4 and -12.1 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks even though RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above +4 and WORKPLACES remains below -11, invalidating the joint suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp recent drop in PARKS mobility (-19.7 to -33.9 in two weeks) reflects a seasonal or weather-driven shift away from outdoor recreation, which redirects discretionary activity toward indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -19.7 to -33.9 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following the PARKS decline, or both series move in the same direction, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has turned positive and stabilized (-2.0 to +0.4) across the snapshot, indicating normalization of essential-trip mobility that typically precedes and co-moves with broader retail and recreation recovery over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -2.0 to +0.4 over the four-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining positive and stable, breaking the presumed co-movement.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stagnated within a narrow band (-13.4 to -12.1) for four consecutive weeks, signaling that employer return-to-office policies have plateaued; this caps the commute-linked retail footfall that would otherwise drive RETAIL_REC growth.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-over-week change stays below 1.5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES values stayed within a 1.3-point range across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to improve over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES remains flat within the stagnation band.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous stagnation in TRANSIT (around -35 to -37) and WORKPLACES (around -12 to -13) indicates suppressed commuting-linked trip chains that normally combine with retail stops; their joint flatness compounds to hold back RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed between -36.7 and -35.0 and WORKPLACES between -13.4 and -12.1 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining flat within their observed bands, indicating no compounding suppression.

mechanism_narrative: In a cautious-reopening regime, RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above +4% signals continued household risk-aversion; if this persists at the decision point it will cap near-term RETAIL_REC growth over the following week before any broader recovery can take hold.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +4.0 at the decision week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 4.9 at t-0w, matching its t-3w level of 4.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following the snapshot even though RESIDENTIAL stays above +4.0, contradicting the caution-driven cap.
